# tag_audio_files

[← Command index](README.md)

Tag audio files with the right per-genre defaults, then apply them in one run.

## Synopsis

```
tag_audio_files [options]
```

## Description

Runs `audio_metadata_tool`'s `Tag` and `Apply` steps with the settings always used
for the library, so they do not have to be remembered. For each genre it:

1. Reads each album's tags into its JSON file, leaving out comments and forcing the
   `genre` tag to the genre folder's name.
2. Writes the JSON tags back into the audio files, unless `--no_apply` is given.

The one per-genre difference is track numbering. Genres downloaded from YouTube by
`download_audio_files` carry meaningless, identical track numbers, so their tracks are
renumbered by file order. The genres treated this way are listed in
`audio_track_index_genres` in `Shared/joybox/config/audio.py` (`ASMR` and `Story`);
every other genre keeps its track numbers.

Albums are found as in `audio_metadata_tool`, and without `-g` every genre with albums
is processed. Use `audio_metadata_tool` directly for `Clear` or other settings.

## Options

### Selection

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-g, --genre <genre>` | Genre folder under `Music` to process; every genre with albums when omitted. Allowed: `ASMR`, `Audiobook`, `Classical`, `Game`, `Radio`, `Regular`, `Soundtrack`, `Story`, `Therapy`. |
| `-b, --album <album>` | Name of the one album folder to process; every album in the genre when omitted. |
| `-r, --artist <artist>` | Artist folder that holds the `-b` album, for albums stored as `<artist>/<album>`. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--set <set>` | Force an extra tag to a value on every track, as `field=value`; repeat for more fields, e.g. `--set album_artist="Various Artists"`. |
| `--clear_existing` | Remove each file's existing tags before writing the ones from the JSON. |
| `--no_apply` | Write the JSON metadata files only; do not change the audio files. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Tag and apply the Story genre (renumbered by file order)

```bash
tag_audio_files -g Story
```

### Tag and apply the whole library

```bash
tag_audio_files
```

### Preview tagging a genre without writing anything

```bash
tag_audio_files -g Story -p -v
```

### Tag and apply one album

```bash
tag_audio_files -g Regular -b "Some Album"
```

### Force an extra field on top of the defaults

```bash
tag_audio_files -g Soundtrack --set album_artist="Various Artists"
```

### Write the JSON files only, leaving the audio files alone

```bash
tag_audio_files -g ASMR --no_apply
```

## Notes

- `tag_audio_files -g Story` is the same as `audio_metadata_tool -a Tag -g Story --exclude_comments --set genre=Story --use_index_for_track_number` followed by `audio_metadata_tool -a Apply -g Story`.
- `--set genre=...` replaces the automatic genre. Use `--set` for other fields; it accepts the same fields as `audio_metadata_tool --set`.
- A genre with no albums is skipped with a warning.
